He also experienced alcohol withdrawal and mental status changes. Following aggressive thiamine repletion and electrolyte correction, he developed aspiration pneumonia and subsequent mental status deterioration, leading to a diagnosis of Central Pontine Myelinolysis (CPM). He was treated with antibiotics, anti-seizure medications, and supportive care including nutritional support via NG tube and later PEG tube. His weakness improved to 4-6/5 strength, and he was discharged to rehabilitation. He requires ongoing neurological follow-up and physical therapy.

The patient needs to discuss continuing nutritional status and blood counts with their Oncologist and their GI doctor. A follow-up appointment with the Oncologist is scheduled for December 19th at 3:30 pm. The patient will be started on oral vancomycin and omeprazole.

No organism was identified as the etiology of her pneumonia.

The patient was maintained on prednisone and Mestinon at her home doses. She did well and had no complications from her myasthenia. She will be followed as an outpatient. She was started on Bactrim for pneumocystis prophylaxis given her chronic steroid use.
